h: Rock Gardens, Winter Colour and a Station Shortcut
p: Once you're through the gates, a few spots deserve a detour. The rock garden is a lovely little world of alpine plants tucked among the stones, the lake brings in ducks and reflections, and the Systematic Beds lay out plant families in neat order, the way Henslow's teaching garden intended. The Scented Garden is a treat for anyone who likes to stop and sniff, and it's a great one for children, who can be set the challenge of finding the strongest smell.

Don't write the garden off in the colder months, either. The Winter Garden is planted for coloured stems, bark and early flowers, so there's real colour even when the rest of Cambridge looks grey. A crisp, sunny winter morning here can be every bit as good as a June afternoon.

Allow a couple of hours, more if you're keen photographers or plant nerds. Arriving by train? The garden sits between the station and the city centre, so it makes a gorgeous green route into town rather than plodding along the main roads. Bring a flask and a snack in the cooler months, and pop the Scott Polar Research Institute's museum on Lensfield Road on your list too, as it's only a short walk away.
